firmware.title: Bluetooth Firmware Selection
firmware.invalid: %s is not a Realtek firmware file: probably a web page was saved instead of the file. Download it again with the 'plain' link and replace it.
firmware.rom_running: Could not connect: the adapter's firmware is not loaded. Put the files shown on the Adapter screen into the firmware folder, press Restart Bluetooth and connect again.
firmware.rom_status: The firmware is not loaded, so the adapter cannot connect or stream. Put the files shown on the Adapter screen into the firmware folder; Bluetooth then starts again with them.
firmware.rom_short: The adapter cannot connect or stream until these files are there.
firmware.manual_instructions:
1. Click 'Open Download Page' to open kernel.org
2. Download the fw and config files
3. Click 'Open Firmware Folder' and place the files there
firmware.vendor_intel: Intel adapter (experimental). AX210 and newer are not supported. If it starts in bootloader mode, see the setup guide.
firmware.vendor_broadcom: Broadcom adapter (experimental): no Realtek files needed.
firmware.vendor_csr: CSR adapter: no firmware files needed.
firmware.auto_no_adapter: No adapter detected. Bind it to WinUSB with Zadig; Auto then picks the chip when it is connected.
firmware.auto_unrecognized: The adapter was not recognized. If it has a Realtek chip, choose the chip; otherwise choose Not Realtek.
firmware.vendor_unsupported: This adapter needs a firmware loader that A2DP Windows Bridge does not have (MediaTek / Qualcomm), so A2DP Windows Bridge cannot use it.
firmware.download_explain: Downloads these files from kernel.org and saves them in the firmware folder.
firmware.download_license: The files are Realtek's proprietary firmware, redistributable under the terms in linux-firmware's WHENCE and LICENCE.rtlwifi_firmware.txt. Download them only if you accept those terms.
firmware.downloaded: Firmware downloaded. Bluetooth loads it at the next connection.
firmware.downloading: Downloading the firmware from kernel.org… This can take up to a minute.
firmware.download_slow: The download is taking a while. It goes on in the background.
firmware.download_failed: Could not download the firmware (no connection to kernel.org, or a file did not match). Use Open Download Page to get the files yourself.

receiver.title: Peer Receiver Test
receiver.intro: Streams to tools/linux_sink/a2dpwb_sink.py on another PC and compares what was sent with what arrived.
receiver.address_hint: empty = find on the local network
receiver.address_tooltip: IP address or host name, optionally with :port.
receiver.searching: Looking for a receiver on the local network...
receiver.state_failed: Sending failed: %s Check the distance to the receiver and press Start again.
receiver.state_ready: Ready. Start sends to the receiver's Bluetooth adapter.
receiver.state_connecting: Connecting to the receiver over Bluetooth...
receiver.state_waiting: Waiting for audio to arrive at the receiver...
receiver.mtu_tooltip: MTU the receiver offers: 672 as BlueZ, 679 the smallest LDAC accepts, 895 / 1005 common.
receiver.log_start: Start: send %s, %s, %s, %s, %s to %s; receiver MTU %s, buffer %s
receiver.log_configure_failed: the receiver did not confirm the settings (older a2dpwb_sink?)
receiver.log_link_lost: Bluetooth connection lost, A2DP Windows Bridge reconnects
receiver.source_tooltip: Test tone keeps the stream steady. With System audio, silence counts as a pause.
receiver.afh_tooltip: Auto avoids this PC's 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channel. Manual: enter channels, e.g. 6,11.
receiver.help: Counts start with each stream and at Reset. Dropout: the buffer would have run dry. Skip: it would have overfilled.

capture.auto_switch: Set as Windows default output while connected
capture.volume_sync_hint: The audio device's volume and the Windows volume move together.
capture.virtual_supported: VB-Cable (not installed) and other virtual devices also work as Output Source
capture.app_hint: If an app is missing, start playback in it and click Refresh.
capture.hint_loopback: Sends everything the Windows default output plays. It keeps playing there too; mute it in Windows to hear only the headphones.
capture.hint_virtual: Records what apps play into the selected device.
capture.hint_app: Sends only what the selected app plays. It keeps playing on its own output too.
tooltip.abr: Adjusts quality to the connection. LHDC V5 ABR ignores the quality setting and stays at 400 kbps or below.
tooltip.codec_fallback_help:
The device did not offer %s when connecting, so %s is used.

Disconnect it from other phones or PCs and connect again. On Sony devices, also turn off "Connect to 2 devices simultaneously".
tooltip.sample_rate: Auto: 48 kHz, or the best rate the device takes. Higher rates use more bandwidth.
tooltip.bit_depth: 24-bit is for LDAC and LHDC V5.

ui.dev.intro: For finding out why a device stays silent. Changes apply when the next stream starts.
ui.dev.active: Overrides are on. Turn them off before reporting a problem.
ui.dev.packet_dump_hint: Size, timestamp and first bytes, in the log.
ui.dev.aac_config_bitrate0_hint: Sends 0 (unknown) as the bit rate when it configures the audio device.
ui.dev.aac_latm_v0_hint: AudioMuxVersion 0 with implicit signaling, instead of the format Android and PipeWire send.
ui.dev.aac_bitrate_hint: 32 to 512; empty = the highest bit rate the device takes. Still limited by the media payload.
ui.dev.log_intro: Applies while developer mode is on.
ui.dev.log_day_cap_hint: 10 to 10240 (default 100). Above it, debug and trace lines stop until the next day.
ui.dev.log_always_hint: No time limit, and on from start-up.
ui.dev.log_trace_warn: Trace logs every HCI and media packet: hundreds of MB an hour, up to the daily size limit.
ui.dev.log_health_hint: For the whole stream, not only its first minute.
ui.dev.mark_hint: Marks the moment in the log, e.g. when the stutter starts.

ui.adapter.ids_unknown: Shown once this adapter has been used.
ui.adapter.experimental_hint: Tried on only a few adapters so far.
ui.adapter.assign_title: Let A2DP Windows Bridge use this adapter
ui.adapter.assign_explain: Windows stops using this adapter, so devices paired through it stop working until you restore the driver. Other Bluetooth adapters are not affected.
ui.adapter.assign_short: Replaces the original driver: Windows will no longer use this adapter for Bluetooth
ui.adapter.assign_unsupported: A2DP Windows Bridge cannot use this adapter, so its driver stays as it is

ui.adapter.restore_explain: Windows can use the adapter again. A2DP Windows Bridge cannot stream through it until WinUSB is assigned again.
ui.adapter.restore_short: Gives the adapter back to Windows' Bluetooth
ui.adapter.assigned_restart: %s now uses the WinUSB driver. Unplug it and plug it back in (built-in adapter: restart Windows) before connecting.
ui.adapter.restart_needed_hint: Windows has not loaded the driver yet. Unplug the adapter and plug it back in; for a built-in adapter, restart Windows.
ui.adapter.restored: %s is back on its original driver
ui.adapter.afh_bad: Enter Wi-Fi channels from 1 to 14, e.g. 6,11

ui.setup.title: Set up A2DP Windows Bridge
ui.setup.intro: Three steps to hear your PC on your audio devices.
ui.setup.adapter_intro: A2DP Windows Bridge needs a USB Bluetooth adapter of its own. Choose the one to use.
ui.setup.unsupported_note: A2DP Windows Bridge cannot use MediaTek or Qualcomm adapters. Choose another, such as a Realtek one.
ui.setup.driver_ok: The adapter is ready for A2DP Windows Bridge
ui.setup.auto_explain: A2DP Windows Bridge needs this adapter to itself. One click sets it up:
ui.setup.auto_will_driver: Switches it to the WinUSB driver. Windows stops using this adapter until you give it back on the Adapters screen. Other adapters keep working.
ui.setup.auto_driver: Switching the driver… Windows may ask for permission.
ui.setup.auto_failed: The adapter could not be set up
ui.setup.auto_advanced: To do these steps one by one (driver, firmware, manual download), use the Adapters screen.
ui.setup.device_intro: Put the audio device in pairing mode and press Connect.

ui.v1_running.title: Another A2DP Windows Bridge is running
ui.v1_running.text: Two copies cannot share the Bluetooth adapter. Exit the other one from its tray icon.

tooltip.vbr: Uses a variable bit rate if the device supports it. Only when AAC is chosen by name, not Auto.
tooltip.sbc_bitpool: Higher sounds better and needs a higher bit rate (%d-%d). Auto: the highest.
tooltip.sbc_abr: Lowers the bitpool when the connection falls behind, then raises it again. Only when SBC or SBC XQ is chosen by name.
tooltip.sbc_bitpool_live: SBC bitpool in use / the stream's highest. ABR moves it between %u and %u.
error.sbc_bitpool_range: Enter a bitpool from %d to %d, or Auto
